content: The title of the page should be formatted as (Disease name) electrocardiogram, with only the first letter of the title capitalized. The primary objective of the page is to describe and provide examples of key electrocardiographic (EKG) findings that may be observed in the disease being discussed. At the top of the edit box, include the {{CMG}} template, your name template, and the microchapter navigation template that was created initially. When creating hyperlinks within Wikidoc, enclose key terms in brackets to link them to other pages. For instance, if the text includes the term anterior spinal artery syndrome, the hyperlink should direct to anterior spinal artery syndrome rather than generic terms like anterior, artery, or syndrome. For further guidance on creating links, refer to the provided instructions. Adhere to the formatting and capitalization rules outlined in the template. The disease name should be included in the first sentence of every subsection. In the overview section, the disease name must appear in the first sentence. This section aims to summarize the EKG findings in a few sentences. It can mirror the EKG segment from the overview page. For an example of an overview section on an electrocardiogram page, refer to the provided link. If there are no EKG findings associated with the disease, state: There are no ECG findings associated with (Disease Name). If an EKG is useful for diagnosis, state: An ECG may be helpful in the diagnosis of (Disease Name). Findings on an EKG that are suggestive of or diagnostic of the disease should be listed explicitly. In the section titled Key EKG Findings in (Disease Name), provide visual examples of EKG patterns associated with the disease. Recommended sources for images include RadsWiki, the National Library of Medicine, Wikipedia, or Radiopaedia. For instructions on inserting images, refer to the provided link. If there are no indications for obtaining an EKG in a specific condition, write: There are no clear indications to obtain an ECG in patients with (Disease Name). If the disease is not associated with specific EKG findings, write: (Disease Name) is not associated with specific ECG findings, and ECG may not be helpful in the diagnosis or management of this condition. When presenting EKG examples, follow this specific order: description of the finding, the image, the source of the image, and then a line break. The description of the image should clearly convey the condition and include hyperlinks for key terms to enhance searchability. Provide a detailed description of the key EKG findings observed in the disease, including any sub-classifications or associated conditions. The description should specify the heart rate, rhythm, segment changes, and any special waves (e.g., delta waves in Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome). If the image lacks a description, use the name of the image instead. The size of the EKG image should be 800 pixels. If this size does not fit within the template, reduce it to 500 pixels. Cite the source of the image as demonstrated in the example provided. If there are more than four EKG examples for a single disease, create a separate page titled (Disease Name) EKG examples. Additionally, add an indented tab for this page under the Electrocardiogram section in the microchapter navigation template.
